rewrites.summary:
For a trans visitor, the risk picture here is the national baseline plus a small deduction: no trans-specific incident, court ruling, or enforcement failure originating in Arica y Parinacota is identified in any cited source, and the dossier's one hard legal finding — the appeals-court annulment holding that the 'femicide' offence protects only 'a person biologically female' — was delivered in the neighbouring region, not here. The worse-than-national grouping rests on a shared judicial climate rather than on a local ruling.

Practical exposure is not materially different from the national baseline: the region held a 0.84 % share of nationally documented anti-LGBTI cases in 2024 — the smallest deviation (−0.03 against the national 0.72) in the scored set — and an earlier annual survey recorded its complaints rising around 300 % against 2020 amid a national decline. No positive institutional finding is documented (no diversity office, no municipal ordinance, no court protection), and a local free legal-aid channel for discrimination complaints has existed as a mitigation resource since 2017.

No source addresses border-screening, document handling, or marriage/partner-travel consequences specific to trans visitors here; the visitor assessment rests on the national legal framework and these regional signals.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
The dossier bases the worse-than-national grouping on the shared judicial geography of the northern courts' non-recognition of trans women as women; the Iquique Court of Appeals annulment that anchors that framing was delivered in the neighbouring region of Tarapacá, and no named local finding evidences the context in Arica y Parinacota.

Score context: at 0.69 the region sits 0.05 above Tarapacá, the compared region (0.64), which produced the femicide-annulment ruling, and 0.02 above Ñuble, the other compared region (0.67), whose sharper statistical signal is a +300 % surge against this region's sub-percent case share; versus the national 0.72 the deviation is −0.03, the smallest in the scored set.

National survey context: increases in recorded homo/transphobia cases in most regions outside the metropolitan core were reported for both the 2024 and 2025 annual surveys, and the 2021-data cycle recorded the first national drop in eight years (−12 %) alongside rises in five regions — with the national decline tied to visibility won in the year equal marriage was approved.
rewrites.localsOnly:
The free legal-aid service for sexual-orientation and gender-identity discrimination cases operates in the region since November 2017 — Arica y Parinacota became the fourth jurisdiction where the foundation provides this support — under a collaboration with pro-bono lawyer Piera Balbontin Nef covering the region's jurisdiction. The foundation's legal director said discrimination is greater in regions far from the capital, which is why local legal support matters.

Institutional absence: no diversity office, no municipal ordinance, and no documented court protection are recorded for the region.

No source documents border-screening practice, document handling, or marriage/partner-travel consequences for trans visitors in this region, so the visitor picture rests on the national legal framework and the regional case-share signals alone.

The 0.84 % share (2024 data) and the around-300 % increase (2021 data, published 2022) come from different survey cycles and are not directly comparable; neither figure is independently verified by a region-specific source. The deviation rests on a shared judicial-climate framing whose only concrete ruling was delivered in the neighbouring region, and no trans-specific incident, court ruling, or enforcement failure originating here is documented to confirm the framing locally.

blindSourceSummaries: Crime-desk news report: the appeals court annulled the entire trial over the killing of a transgender woman, holding that the nation's 'femicide' offence protects only 'a person biologically female', so the conviction could not stand as framed — the dossier's cited basis for grouping this state/province with its neighbour as worse than national on shared judicial geography, while the ruling itself belongs to the neighbour.

Annual human-rights report on sexual and gender diversity (2024 data, published March 2025): 2,847 recorded cases nationally (+78.7 %), with this state/province holding a 0.84 % share — among the lowest — in a year that saw increases in 11 of 16 regions; a small-share state/province where a single case dominates the rate.

Leftist news outlet (2021 data, published April 2022): nationwide homo/transphobia complaints fell 12 %, the first drop in eight years, but in five regions they rose and this state/province was one, its reports climbing around 300 % against 2020; the national decline was tied to visibility won in the year equal marriage was approved — regional complaint data running against the national trend.

Foundation announcement (2017): this state/province became one of the first jurisdictions where the foundation provides free legal aid for sexual-orientation and gender-identity discrimination cases, via a collaboration with a pro-bono lawyer; its legal director said discrimination is greater in regions far from the capital, which is why local legal support matters — an accessible local complaint channel complementing the national anti-discrimination framework.
